marks.gloss_en: איתמר נמי -- Rebbi's statement, via Ravin's chain, is word for word Rava's re-told one (no SupportKind names איתמר נמי)
Rebbi (via Ravin's chain): they taught only where he did not designate it for insulating
תניא נמי הכי: heftek fleece is not moved; if the householder prepared it, it is moved
בשל הפתק שנו -- the mishna's 'one does not move it' speaks of merchant's-shelf fleece (= p_ravina_shel_heftek)
Ravina: they taught [the mishna's 'one does not move it'] of fleece from a merchant's shelf (heftek)
הוא דאמר כי האי תנא, דתניא: if he went out in them a while before dark, he may go out in them (no SupportKind names כי האי תנא)
הוא דאמר כי האי תנא -- he spoke as the tanna of the pakorin baraita
the baraita: one goes out with pakorin and combed wool when he dipped them in oil and wrapped them with twine
אף אנן נמי תנינא: if a pillow or sheet was on the straw before dark, he shakes it with his hand -- שמע מינה
the mishna: straw on a bed -- he may not shake it with his hand, but he shakes it with his body
דכי אתא רב דימי ... R' Chanina ben Akiva told his students: go out and think [of the branches]
the stam: the tanna who disputes RSBG is R' Chanina ben Akiva
מדקאמר אי בית המשתה אי בית האבל -- thought sufficed only where they were preoccupied; ordinarily, tied yes, untied no: he is the tanna who requires tying
the stam: [thinking sufficed] specifically in a house of mourning or of feasting, because they are preoccupied
דאי כרבנן -- האמרי בעינן מעשה: if it were the Rabbanan's, they require an action
the Rabbanan before Rav Pappa: [the designated-corner ruling] is as RSBG
אפילו תימא רבנן -- they require an action only for a thing on which one can be done (= p_rav_pappa_bar_maaseh)
Rav Pappa: the Rabbanan require an action only for a thing on which an action can be done; for a thing on which none can be done, no
בשלמא Rav as the tanna kamma and Shmuel as RSBG; but Rav Asi -- like whom?
the stam: Rav spoke as the tanna kamma
if baraita A is R' Shimon's, say the seifa: but he may not wash his hair with them -- and R' Shimon permits it, דתנן: a nazir washes and parts his hair
baraita A, seifa: but he may not wash his hair with them
Rava (re-told): they taught [that fleece is not moved] only where he did not designate it for insulating
palm branches cut for wood, about which he reconsidered [and decided] to sit [on them]: he must tie [them]
Shmuel: he thinks [of sitting on them] -- thought suffices
Rav Yehuda: a person brings in his basket full of earth and does all his needs with it
baraita A: one cleans vessels with anything, except silver vessels with gartekon
baraita B: natron and sand are forbidden
the stam: the permitting baraita (A) is R' Shimon's
an unintended act is forbidden
